subject.title: Write tool lacks append mode — isolated cron sessions destroy shared files

question: Should OpenClaw add append support to the existing built-in `write` tool, or should maintainers choose a separate append tool/API before resolving this data-loss issue?
rationale: Current evidence supports the data-loss problem, but the fix changes a public model-facing tool contract and the open implementation PR is now a maintainer API-shape and branch-refresh decision.

options.title: Accept append on write
options.body: Refresh and review the linked PR as the canonical path, preserving overwrite as the default and adding explicit append behavior for ordinary agent and cron writes.

options.title: Use separate append surface
options.body: Ask for a replacement design with a dedicated append tool or different mode contract if maintainers want overwrite and append to be more visibly distinct.

options.title: Defer core change
options.body: Keep the current memory-flush-only wrapper and external backup/workaround guidance while leaving ordinary writes overwrite-only for now.

recommendation.title: Accept append on write
recommendation.body: Refresh and review the linked PR as the canonical path, preserving overwrite as the default and adding explicit append behavior for ordinary agent and cron writes.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared write-tool contract traces through the internalized agent runtime work, making this the strongest routing candidate for the API decision.
